native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the joint PCA of the forms of capital in hundred-year time slices (12 capital Z-variables, 39 slices 4300-500 BCE; PC1 explains 31.8%), the PC1 value at the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age, 1100 BCE (+4.452), is the global maximum of the entire series (97.4th percentile, z=+2.38), and it decisively exceeds every subsequent time horizon 1000-500 BCE (1000=+2.17, 900=+1.65, 800=+1.91, 700=+1.25, 600=+0.83, 500=+0.82; mean +1.44): difference PC1(1100)-mean(1000-500)=+3.01 and 1100 is higher than each of the six points by +2.28 to +3.64. The 1100 BCE peak is driven by simultaneously elevated economic capital (copper/gold 2.85, depot/hoard 3.38, dagger 1.10) and symbolic/social capital (house size 1.65, monuments 1.35). After this, PC1 drops sharply at 1000 BCE and drifts slowly downward at about -0.28/century toward 500 BCE, i.e. capital-accumulation levels remain low throughout 1000-500 BCE. A robustness PCA restricted to the YBA window confirms the same direction (1100=+4.07 > all six subsequent points; mean(1000-500)=-0.68; diff +4.75).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load capital.csv (European decimal): 39 century slices (4300-500 BCE), 12 capital Z-variables, verified identical to the century-point raw Z values in time_series_data.csv (max diff 0.0). 2) Joint PCA via scipy SVD on centered (not re-scaled) variables; fix PC1 sign so ZCU_AU loading is positive. 3) Read PC1 at 1100,1000,900,800,700,600,500 BCE; compare via (a) difference vs mean(1000-500)=+3.014, (b) per-point differences, (c) linear slope (-0.28/century) and point-to-point changes; position 1100 as percentile/z within full series (97.4%, z+2.38) and within YBA (85.7%, z+2.23). 4) Robustness: YBA-only PCA (drop zero-variance ZSichel, ZKeform) confirms direction (diff +4.75). 5) Capital-form labels (economic/social/symbolic/cultural) are a study-background-based suggested mapping and do not affect the joint-PCA PC1 quantification.
